substantive_nonglyph.observed: Plant/furniture contacts at three domestic support heights organize a complete frontal scene and stepped reading seams.

style.assigned_relationship: Dry drawn frontal domestic section comparing high table, lower sill and floor plant, with broad invitation/body entry and lower identity seam.
style.observed_relationship: Clean dark plant contours, flat clay-red table and teal sill/window/floor planes strengthen the assigned section; invitation, broad prose and first-ledger route remain attached to domestic support edges.
style.remaining_limits: Some leaf-vein/pottery texture remains, and clay-red occupies table/pots rather than a broad wall plane.

exclusion_check.observation: The high table edge is the transition from market to ledger; lower sill is a substantive plant support and identity seam; the tree spans the right structure and floor. These specific domestic positions determine the graphic relationships instead of a subordinate tiny image on a huge title/date board.
exclusion_check.reference_geometry_protection: No client composition preservation condition applies; guide coordinates are planning choices.

hangul_anatomy_spacing.observation: Stable mature Korean sans bodies/counters and ordinary word spaces; consistent prose baselines and readable Latin/numerals.

information_relationship.observation: Invitation, continuous paragraph, slogan and market share a left start; nearby date/hours/place and access/care/URL follow the high ledge. Quiet lower identity does not break that route.

function_contact.observation: Table pot/saucer, sill pot and floor pot/saucer touch supports; upright table legs reach the floor. No human action or functional mechanism is claimed.

material_edge_finish.observation: Cleaner architectural boundaries and flatter leaf contours; pot rims and bases are defined. Local clay texture and leaf detail remain.

observations.location: Table, sill and floor plant contacts
observations.observation: The medium plant's clay pot and saucer rest on the table edge; the small round-leaf pot rests on the lower thick sill; a large clay pot with a distinct saucer rests on the floor. Upright table legs, window structure and floor are continuous.

observations.location: Invitation through paragraph and visit ledger
observations.observation: Large invitation enters the broad three-line explanation. Shared left start carries slogan and market name to table edge; date, hours and venue occupy one readable baseline under it. Access/care and URL remain adjacent and readable.

High table and lower sill form a stepped shape; three plant sizes are distinct and a tall right tree reaches through the upper/right crop to its floor pot. Quiet lower identity sits below the sill seam.

All twelve entries are planar mature sans with visible counters, stable Hangul bodies and ordinary word spaces; prose wraps at meaningful phrase boundaries into three lines. URL is intact and appears once. Thin dividers between date/hours/venue contain no extra lettering.

Compared with initial, foliage has stronger dark boundary lines and more open branch intervals; leafy wall shadows are removed. Clay-red tabletop and legs are flatter, teal sill/window/floor shapes have cleaner boundaries. Some pot surface marks and leaf vein lines remain.

Hard geometric window shadows replace the initial botanical watercolor shadowing. The stepped domestic supports still organize the copy route; the diagonal shadow is secondary to table/sill/floor contacts.

residuals.issue: Pot texture and selected leaf-vein marks remain; contour treatment is cleaner and more polished than rough charcoal.
Clay-red remains concentrated in the table edge, legs and pottery rather than a large wall plane; teal provides the larger architectural mass.

decision.reason: Retains exact readable copy and three-height domestic reading route while strengthening the assigned drawing and planar furniture; no further invocation is needed for the remaining local surface detail.
